title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated video and fabricated social media profiles were used to make a real, named attorney appear to be offering immigration legal services he never offered. The failure did not occur inside a deployed AI product belonging to a legitimate organisation. Instead, AI tools were used by external bad actors to manufacture convincing likeness content at scale, producing thousands of fake profiles across multiple platforms before detection.

The platform-level failure is one of moderation lag. Nearly 6,500 fake profiles accumulated across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram before removal, and removal required the real attorney to hire a private anti-piracy company rather than relying on the platforms' own detection systems. The vector used to collect money, WhatsApp combined with peer-to-peer payment apps, sat entirely outside any environment where a legal-services check could have intervened. A routine verification step, confirming that a social media account or video is associated with a licensed professional before it promotes legal services, is not established as having existed here.

What is not established is who is responsible for creating or operating the scheme, where it originated, or whether any platform was aware of the fraud before the attorney's intervention. Reports describe losses and profile volumes as stated by the attorney and investigators, but no finding or charge had been publicly confirmed at the time of reporting.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
# Summary

Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the victim of an extensive AI-powered identity theft scheme targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos using Leal's likeness to promote fraudulent immigration services, including false promises of US residency for $2,200 payments. The scam escalated dramatically over the past three months, with scammers directing victims through WhatsApp to exchange phony contracts and collect money via Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App.

After discovering the fraud when potential clients called his office, Leal hired an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The videos falsely feature supposed former clients praising Leal's services and claim he can secure the release of detainees for specific fees. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to launch an investigation into the scams' origin.
